seoTitle: Free Bech32 and Bech32m Decoder and Encoder
metaDescription: Decode and validate bech32 or bech32m strings such as SegWit and Taproot addresses, or encode hex bytes and witness programs. Free, in your browser.
intro: Paste a bech32 or bech32m string to decode it, or switch the mode to encode hex bytes or a SegWit witness program. The tool shows checksum validity, the human-readable part and the data.
why: Bitcoin SegWit and Taproot addresses, Lightning invoices and several other protocols use bech32 encoding, which has a built-in checksum designed to catch typing errors. When you build wallet software or inspect a transaction, you need to know whether an address is valid, which checksum variant it uses and what witness version and program sit inside. Version 0 addresses use bech32, while later versions use bech32m, and mixing them up is a classic bug. This tool decodes both, reports rule violations such as a wrong program length, and recognises P2WPKH, P2WSH and P2TR forms. It can also encode. Everything runs in your browser; it validates format only and does not check the network or funds.
howTo: Choose a mode: decode, encode bytes or encode segwit.
Paste the bech32 string, or the hex bytes or witness program to encode.
For encoding, set the human-readable part, checksum type or witness version, then read the result.

faq.q: What is the difference between bech32 and bech32m?
faq.a: They use different checksum constants. SegWit version 0 addresses use bech32, and version 1 and later, including Taproot, use bech32m. Using the wrong one makes the address invalid.

faq.q: Why does it reject a long string?
faq.a: Standard bech32 is limited to 90 characters. Tick 'No 90-character limit' for formats such as Lightning invoices that exceed it.

faq.q: Does a valid checksum mean the address is safe to use?
faq.a: No. It only means the string is well formed. It says nothing about who controls the address, which network it belongs to beyond the prefix, or whether funds will arrive.

faq.q: Can it decode other data besides addresses?
faq.a: Yes. Any bech32 or bech32m string is decoded to its 5-bit values and, if they fit whole bytes, the bytes. The SegWit analysis only appears when the first value is a valid witness version.
